/-- This formalization-only auxiliary records that the error parameter of a supplied
`CombinedPointsWitness` is nonnegative. It supports `lem:qld-4-10`, paper lines
689--709, and does not construct or assert existence of the witness. -/
theorem CombinedPointsWitness.delta_nonneg {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaQ : ℝ}
    {setting : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
    (points : CombinedPointsWitness setting deltaQ) :
    0 ≤ deltaQ := by
  exact le_trans
    (DistanceCalculus.opFamilyDistSq_nonneg
      (uniformDistribution
        ((Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)))
      (fun xz ab => setting.place .AA' ((points.Q .alice xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
      (fun xz ab => setting.place .BA'' ((points.Q .bob xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
      setting.psiHat)
    (points.self_consistent .AA' .BA'' trivial)

namespace ExtendedLineGame

variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaQ deltaL : ℝ}
variable {setting : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
variable {points : CombinedPointsWitness setting deltaQ}

/-- This formalization-only auxiliary records nonnegativity of the completed
`AA'`--`BA''` line-point defect for a supplied `ExtendedLinesWitness`. It supports
`lem:qld-4-13`, paper lines 1020--1034, by expressing the correlation terms as
those of genuine POVMs on `pairState setting`; it does not construct the witness. -/
theorem completedLinePointDefect_aaBa_nonneg
    (lines : ExtendedLinesWitness setting points deltaL)
    (mu : Distribution
      (DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ×
        (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))) :
    0 ≤ completedLinePointDefect lines .AA' .BA'' mu := by
  let lineMeasurement :
      (DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ×
        (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) →
        Measurement (Option (PauliScalar P)) (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace .alice) :=
    fun sample =>
      (lines.Qline .alice sample.1).postprocess
        (fun coeffs => (directEvalOpt sample.1 sample.2 coeffs).map
          (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P))
  let pointMeasurement :
      (DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ×
        (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) →
        Measurement (Option (PauliScalar P)) (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace .bob) :=
    fun sample =>
      (points.Q .bob
        (projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
        (projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))).postprocess fun values =>
          some (directPointToPauli P sample.2 (alphaVar P.m) * values.1 +
            directPointToPauli P sample.2 (betaVar P.m) * values.2)
  change 0 ≤ consistencyDefect mu
    (fun sample answer => setting.place .AA' ((lineMeasurement sample).effect answer))
    (fun sample answer => setting.place .BA'' ((pointMeasurement sample).effect answer))
    setting.psiHat
  unfold consistencyDefect avgOver
  refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun sample _ =>
    mul_nonneg (mu.nonnegative sample) ?_
  refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun answerA _ => ?_
  refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun answerB _ => ?_
  by_cases hab : answerA = answerB
  · simp [hab]
  · simp only [hab, if_false, DistanceCalculus.consistency_term_eq_stateQForm]
    rw [← stateQForm_pairState_eq_AA'_BA'' setting
      ((lineMeasurement sample).effect answerA)
      ((pointMeasurement sample).effect answerB)
      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
        ((lineMeasurement sample).pos answerA)).isHermitian
      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
        ((pointMeasurement sample).pos answerB)).isHermitian]
    exact DistanceCalculus.stateQForm_nonneg (pairState setting)
      (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg
        ((lineMeasurement sample).pos answerA)
        ((pointMeasurement sample).pos answerB))

end ExtendedLineGame

/-- This formalization-only auxiliary records that the error parameter of a supplied
`ExtendedLinesWitness` is nonnegative. It supports `lem:qld-4-13`, paper lines
1020--1034, and does not construct or assert existence of the witness. -/
theorem ExtendedLinesWitness.delta_nonneg {P : AdmissibleParams}
    {epsilon deltaQ deltaL : ℝ} {setting : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon}
    {points : CombinedPointsWitness setting deltaQ}
    (lines : ExtendedLinesWitness setting points deltaL) :
    0 ≤ deltaL := by
  exact le_trans
    (ExtendedLineGame.completedLinePointDefect_aaBa_nonneg lines
      (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd))
    lines.consistent_alice

end

   174		$\E_{u,u'} d_\rho(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'},
   175		\mathcal{O}^{u+u'})^2 \le 2\delta$. No commutation among the
   176		observables is used.
   177	
   178		\emph{The Fourier-square measurement and its Naimark rounding.} By
   179		Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform} the operators
   180		$B^v = (\widehat{\mathcal{O}}^v)^2$ are positive semidefinite and sum to
   181		$\Id$, so they form a POVM indexed by $\F_2^t$.
   182		Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper}, applied with an ancillary space $\hilb'$
   183		of dimension $2^t + 1$ and with $\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ the basis vector of
   184		its extra direction, produces orthogonal projectors on $\hilb \ot \hilb'$
   185		compressing along $\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ to the $B^v$; the residual
   186		projector of the construction is folded into the outcome $v = 0$, which
   187		gives a projective measurement $\{C^v\}$ resolving the identity on
   188		$\hilb \ot \hilb'$ whose compression is still $\{B^v\}$, because the
   189		$B^v$ themselves sum to $\Id$. Set
   190		$\mathcal{L}^u = \sum_v \chi_v(u) \, C^v$. Each $\mathcal{L}^u$ is
   191		Hermitian, and the orthogonality of the $C^v$ together with
   192		$\chi_v(u) \chi_v(u') = \chi_v(u+u')$ gives
   193		$\mathcal{L}^u \mathcal{L}^{u'} = \mathcal{L}^{u+u'}$ for all $u, u'$;
   194		in particular $(\mathcal{L}^u)^2 = \mathcal{L}^0 = \sum_v C^v = \Id$,
   195		so the $\mathcal{L}^u$ are binary observables.
   196	
   197		\emph{The distance/defect identity.} Since $\mathcal{L}^u$ and
   198		$\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id$ are binary observables and $\rho'$ is a density
   199		operator, Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance} gives
   200		$d_{\rho'}(\mathcal{L}^u, \mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id)^2
   201		= 2 - 2 \Re \Tr(\mathcal{L}^u (\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id) \rho')$.
   202		Compressing along $\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$,
   203		$\Re \Tr(\mathcal{L}^u (\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id) \rho')
   204		= \Re \Tr(\mathcal{O}^u \sum_v \chi_v(u) B^v \rho)$; averaging over $u$
   205		turns $\E_u \chi_v(u) \mathcal{O}^u$ into $\widehat{\mathcal{O}}^v$, and
   206		expanding the three Fourier coefficients and summing the characters
   207		(Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}) gives
   208		\[
   209			\E_u \Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{L}^u (\mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id) \rho'\big)
   210			= \sum_v \Re \Tr\big((\widehat{\mathcal{O}}^v)^3 \rho\big)
   211			= \E_{u,u'} \Re \Tr\big(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'}
   212			\mathcal{O}^{u+u'} \rho\big)\,.
   213		\]
   214		Hence
   215		$\E_u d_{\rho'}(\mathcal{L}^u, \mathcal{O}^u \ot \Id)^2
   216		= 2 - 2 \E_{u,u'} \Re \Tr(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'}
   217		\mathcal{O}^{u+u'} \rho)
   218		= \E_{u,u'} d_\rho(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'},
   219		\mathcal{O}^{u+u'})^2 \le 2\delta$ by the first step. The measurement
   220		form follows by halving, through the normalization identity of
   221		Lemma~\ref{lem:binary-measurement-distance}.
   222	
   223		The obligations attached to the theorem at its point of use --- the
   224		correspondence between the correlation hypothesis above and the relation
   225		$\approx_\delta$ of Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}, the
   226		instantiation of $\rho$ as a reduced state of $\ket{\hat\psi}$, the
   227		absorption of the ancilla register into padding of the strategy state,
   228		and the identity $\mathcal{L}^0 = \Id$ --- are enumerated in
   229		Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-import} and addressed in the proof of
   230		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}.
   231	\end{proof}

   254		$0 \le \delta \le 1$, which would block the fiberwise application

   259		$\mathcal{L}^u = \Id$ for $u = 0$. None of the three is

   672		$\hat{P}_a \hat{P}_b = 0$ for $a \ne b$. Consequently
   673		$Q = \sum_{v \ne 0} \hat{P}_v$ absorbs each of its summands on either

   676		every $\hat{P}_v$ with $v \ne 0$. Splitting off the zero outcome in

   680		identity supplied with the dilation of Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper},

  1053	\section{Applying the classical low-degree test}
  1054	\label{sec:apply-ldt}
  1055	
  1056	The combined point and line measurements of the previous two sections are next
  1057	merged into a single measurement returning a pair of global polynomials that
  1058	encode the $X$-basis and the $Z$-basis information simultaneously. This is
  1059	done by encoding the pair as one polynomial in $2m+2$ variables and invoking
  1060	the quantum soundness of the classical low individual degree test
  1061	(Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}). The classical game, its question
  1062	distribution, and the line-point distribution are defined at dimension $2m+2$
  1063	only when $2m+2$ divides $q$ (Definition~\ref{def:ld-game}), a condition that
  1064	admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ does not supply; the statements below are the
  1065	source statements, without that condition, and their proofs are blocked at
  1066	the instantiation step for admissible parameters with $m \ge 2$. The
  1067	obstruction is recorded in Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility} and
  1068	analyzed, together with candidate repairs, in
  1069	\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}.

  1071	\begin{definition}[The combining map]
  1072		\label{def:combine-map}
  1073		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.combinePoly, MIPStarRE.QPBT.combinePoly_eval}
  1074		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.combinePoly_mem_polyFunc}

  1080		For $f, g \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$, the polynomial
  1081		$\mathrm{combine}_{f,g} \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,2m+2}(\F_q)$ is defined by
  1082		\[
  1083			\mathrm{combine}_{f,g}(x, z, \alpha, \beta)
  1084			= \alpha f(x) + \beta g(z)\,,
  1085			\qquad x \in \F_q^m,\ z \in \F_q^m,\ \alpha \in \F_q,\
  1086			\beta \in \F_q\,.
  1087		\]
  1088		The combining map is also defined for polynomials restricted to lines.
  1089		Let $\ell$ be a line in $\F_q^{2m+2}$ with intercept
  1090		$u = (u_X, u_Z, u_\alpha, u_\beta)$ and slope
  1091		$v = (v_X, v_Z, v_\alpha, v_\beta)$, and let $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ be
  1092		lines in $\F_q^m$ such that for every point
  1093		$(x, z, \alpha, \beta) \in \ell$ it holds that $x \in \ell_X$ and
  1094		$z \in \ell_Z$. Then for any two polynomials
  1095		$f \in \deg_{md}(\ell_X)$ and $g \in \deg_{md}(\ell_Z)$, the polynomial
  1096		$\mathrm{combine}_{f,g} \in \deg_{md+1}(\ell)$ is defined by
  1097		\begin{equation}
  1098			\label{eq:combine-lines}
  1099			\mathrm{combine}_{f,g}(u + t \cdot v)
  1100			= (u_\alpha + t \cdot v_\alpha)\, f(u_X + t \cdot v_X)
  1101			+ (u_\beta + t \cdot v_\beta)\, g(u_Z + t \cdot v_Z)\,,
  1102			\qquad t \in \F_q\,.
  1103		\end{equation}

  1105		polynomials of degree at most $md$ in the line parameter, and each is
  1106		multiplied by an affine factor of degree at most one.

  1258			restricted distribution $D_{\mathrm{ALine},i}$ and
  1259			$D_{\mathrm{DLine},i}$ with error $2m\delta$;

  1261			$D_{\mathrm{Line}} \times D_{\mathrm{Line}}$ holds over any product

  1265			\mathrm{DLine}\}$ and any $i, j \in \{1, \dots, m\}$,

  1270				\sum_{f_X,f_Z}

  1272				\big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}

  1284		axis-parallel and diagonal components and, within each component, uniform
  1285		weight on the index $i$, so each restricted distribution carries mixture
  1286		weight $\tfrac{1}{2m}$ in $D_{\mathrm{Line}}$. A nonnegative average that

  1290		2 applied to the conclusion of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}, whose
  1291		$\simeq_{\delta_P}$ relation over two independent copies of the
  1292		line-point distribution is precisely the statement that the left-hand
  1293		side of \eqref{eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted}, averaged over
  1294		$D_{\mathrm{Line}} \times D_{\mathrm{Line}}$, is at most $\delta_P$.

  1360		$(\ell, u)$ from the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and write
  1361		$u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$, so that Property~1 holds by
  1362		construction; all auxiliary randomness introduced below is sampled
  1363		independently of $(\ell, u)$. We write $\chi$ for the index function of
  1364		Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} at dimension $m$, whose
  1365		classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ for $i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ partition $\F_q$
  1366		into sets of equal size $q/m$, and $\chi_{2m+2}$ for the index function
  1367		at dimension $2m+2$. The function $\chi_{2m+2}$, and with it the
  1368		line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ from which $(\ell, u)$ is
  1369		drawn, is defined only when $2m+2$ divides $q$
  1370		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}); admissibility of
  1371		$(q,m,d)$ supplies only that $m$ divides $q$, and for admissible
  1372		parameters with $m \ge 2$ the required divisibility fails, so this
  1373		first step is an unresolved obligation of the source argument, recorded
  1374		in Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility} and analyzed in
  1375		\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}; the construction below is
  1376		carried out for the parameters for which the distribution is defined.

  1378		\emph{fresh diagonal direction pair} we mean a pair $(s', w')$ with
  1379		$s'$ uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $w' \in \F_q^m$ having coordinates
  1380		$1, \dots, \chi(s')-1$ equal to $0$ and the remaining coordinates
  1381		uniformly random; this is exactly the law of the coordinate--direction
  1382		data of the diagonal component of the line-point distribution over
  1383		$\F_q^m$ (Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}).

  1386		$v = (v_X, v_Z, \alpha_0, \beta_0)$ and $j \in \{1, \dots, 2m+2\}$, set
  1387		$\ell_X = (v'_X, e_{i_X})$ and $\ell_Z = (v'_Z, e_{i_Z})$ where: for
  1388		$1 \le j \le m$, $i_X = j$ and $i_Z$ is uniformly random in
  1389		$\{1,\dots,m\}$; for $m+1 \le j \le 2m$, $i_X$ is uniformly random and
  1390		$i_Z = j - m$; for $2m+1 \le j \le 2m+2$, both $i_X$ and $i_Z$ are
  1391		uniformly random; and $v'_X, v'_Z$ are the canonical line
  1392		representatives of $v_X, v_Z$ for the chosen directions
  1393		(Definition~\ref{def:line-representative}), so that $v_X \in \ell_X$
  1394		and $v_Z \in \ell_Z$.
  1395

  1397		the diagonal component of the line-point distribution
  1398		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} instantiated at
  1399		dimension $2m+2$) the direction $w = (w_X, w_Z, \gamma, \delta)$ has
  1400		coordinates $1, \dots, j-1$ equal to $0$, where $j = \chi_{2m+2}(s)$,
  1401		and its remaining coordinates are uniformly random. These remaining
  1402		coordinates may also vanish, so $w$ need not have a nonzero coordinate

  1404		singleton (Definition~\ref{def:line}).

  1406		% nonzero coordinate is j = chi(s)"
  1407		% (references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, proof

  1409		% property recorded here, which is the one the argument uses. The

  1414		where: for $1 \le j \le m$, $w'_X = w_X$ and $w'_Z = w_Z$, with $s_X$
  1415		uniformly random in the class $\chi^{-1}(j)$ and $s_Z$ uniformly
  1416		random in the class $\chi^{-1}(1)$; for $m+1 \le j \le 2m$, the pair
  1417		$(s_X, w'_X)$ is a fresh diagonal direction pair and $w'_Z = w_Z$,
  1418		with $s_Z$ uniformly random in the class $\chi^{-1}(j-m)$; for
  1419		$2m+1 \le j \le 2m+2$, both $(s_X, w'_X)$ and $(s_Z, w'_Z)$ are fresh
  1420		diagonal direction pairs, sampled independently; and $v'_X, v'_Z$ are
  1421		the canonical representatives of $v_X, v_Z$ for the directions
  1422		$w'_X, w'_Z$.

  1425		axis-parallel, both $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ are constructed to be
  1426		axis-parallel. The containments in Property~2 hold for every point
  1427		$u^\dagger = (u^\dagger_X, u^\dagger_Z, \alpha^\dagger,
  1428		\beta^\dagger)$ of $\ell$: the block $u^\dagger_X$ differs from $v_X$
  1429		by a multiple of the direction of $\ell_X$ when that direction is
  1430		inherited from $\ell$ (namely $e_j$ for axis-parallel $\ell$ with
  1431		$1 \le j \le m$, and $w_X$ for diagonal $\ell$ with $1 \le j \le m$),

  1433		block of the direction of $\ell$ vanishes; in either case

  1435		$u^\dagger_Z \in \ell_Z$.

  1438		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is a function of $\ell$ and of the auxiliary
  1439		randomness alone: the directions used are either read off from the
  1440		direction data of $\ell$ or freshly sampled, and by
  1441		Proposition~\ref{prop:line-equiv} the canonical representatives
  1442		$v'_X, v'_Z$ do not depend on which base point of $\ell$ is used to
  1443		compute them. Under both components of the line-point distribution the
  1444		point $u$ is uniformly distributed on $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and, conditioned
  1445		on the line $\ell$, uniformly distributed on the points of $\ell$
  1446		(each of the $q$ values of the line parameter, or the single point
  1447		when the direction vanishes, being equally likely). Hence, conditioned
  1448		on $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$, the sampled point $u$ is uniformly
  1449		distributed on $\ell$, and it suffices to establish the claimed
  1450		mixture description for the tuple $(\ell_X, \ell_Z, u)$ produced by
  1451		the procedure itself.
  1452	
  1453		Condition on the component of the line-point distribution
  1454		(axis-parallel or diagonal) and on $j$; the mixture of Property~2 is
  1455		over these choices together with the fresh index choices, and the
  1456		blocks $u_X, u_Z$ of $u$ are independent and uniform on $\F_q^m$,
  1457		independent of all direction data. In the axis-parallel case with
  1458		$1 \le j \le m$, the pair $(\ell_X, u_X)$ consists of the uniformly
  1459		random point $u_X$ together with the canonical axis-parallel line
  1460		through it in direction $e_j$, so
  1461		$(\ell_X, u_X) \sim D_{\mathrm{ALine},j}$, while, conditioned
  1462		additionally on $i_Z$, the pair $(\ell_Z, u_Z)$ consists of the
  1463		uniformly random point $u_Z$ together with the canonical line through
  1464		it in direction $e_{i_Z}$, so
  1465		$(\ell_Z, u_Z) \sim D_{\mathrm{ALine},i_Z}$; the two pairs are
  1466		functions of the disjoint independent data $u_X$ and $(u_Z, i_Z)$,
  1467		hence independent. In the diagonal case with $1 \le j \le m$, the
  1468		triple $(u_X, w_X, s_X)$ has $u_X$ uniform, $w_X$ with coordinates
  1469		$1, \dots, j-1$ equal to $0$ and the remaining coordinates uniform,
  1470		and $s_X$ uniform in $\chi^{-1}(j)$, which is exactly the law
  1471		generating $D_{\mathrm{DLine},j}$; hence
  1472		$(\ell_X, u_X) \sim D_{\mathrm{DLine},j}$, and similarly
  1473		$(\ell_Z, u_Z) \sim D_{\mathrm{DLine},1}$ since $w_Z$ is uniform and

  1475		disjoint independent data $(u_X, w_X, s_X)$ and $(u_Z, w_Z, s_Z)$,

  1477		$(\ell_X, u_X)$ and $(\ell_Z, u_Z)$ is either built from the inherited

  1479		direction pair, in which case it is distributed as the uniform mixture

  1481		$\mathrm{v}$; and the two pairs are always functions of disjoint
  1482		independent collections of the variables $u_X$, $u_Z$, the direction

  1484		on the component. Within each component this yields exactly the
  1485		description of Property~2: the pair $(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is

  1487		$D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ and $D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and, conditioned on
  1488		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, each of $u_X$ and $u_Z$ is uniformly distributed

  1490		uniform on the line conditionally on the line. The equivalent product

  2295	\begin{theorem}[Polynomial error after conditioning]
  2296		\label{thm:qld-conditioned-polynomial-bound}
  2297		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_conditioned_polynomial_bound}
  2298		\leanok
  2299		Let $p(x)=\poly(x)$, let $f(x,y)=\poly(x,y)$, and fix $c\ge1$.
  2300		There exists $g(x,y)=\poly(x,y)$ such that for every
  2301		$\eps,\rho\ge0$ and every $\mu\in[1/2,1]$,
  2302		\[
  2303			\min\left\{1,\,
  2304				\mu f\left(\rho,
  2305					\frac{8p(\eps)+c(\eps+\sqrt{\eps})}{\mu}\right)+\rho
  2306			\right\}
  2307			\le g(\eps,\rho).
  2308		\]
  2309		This scalar estimate supports the pasting substitution in the proof of
  2310		Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}. The interval for $\mu$ is an explicit
  2311		hypothesis of this auxiliary estimate.

  2313	\begin{proof}
  2314		\leanok
  2315		Choose $A,r,B,s,t$ as in the polynomial bounds above, and set
  2316		$\alpha=\min\{r,1/2\}$, $\beta=\min\{s,1\}$, and $L=8A+2c$.
  2317		For $0\le\eps,\rho\le1$, the numerator in the argument of $f$ is at
  2318		most $L\eps^\alpha$, and division by $\mu\ge1/2$ costs at most a
  2319		factor of two. The polynomial bound on $f$, together with $\mu\le1$,
  2320		therefore gives the required inequality with
  2321		\[
  2322			g(\eps,\rho)=\bigl(B(1+(2L)^t)+1\bigr)
  2323				\bigl(\eps^{\alpha t}+\rho^\beta\bigr).
  2324		\]
  2325		If either $\eps>1$ or $\rho>1$, this function is at least one, which
  2326		bounds the minimum. All its exponents are positive.
